examples.en: My bag kept getting in the way, so I put it on the floor.
My long hair gets in the way.
Please clear away anything that is in the way.

examples.ko: 좁은 부엌에서 서로 거치적거리지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: In the narrow kitchen, we are careful not to get in each other's way.
The pants were long and got in my way when I walked.
I moved the bags to one side in case they got in the way.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 걸려서 움직임이 불편하거나 일에 방해가 될 때 써요. 비슷한 '방해되다'보다 몸에 걸리는 느낌이 강해요. 사람에게 쓰면 '걸리적거리다'와 마찬가지로 '귀찮게 방해한다'는 거친 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: Use it when something catches on your body or hinders movement or work. It feels more physical, like snagging, than the similar '방해되다'. About a person it sounds harsh, as if they are annoyingly in the way.

examples.en: In the movie, two men fight hand to hand in the street.

examples.ko: 어제 본 영화에서 두 사람이 오랫동안 격투했어요.
examples.en: In the movie I saw yesterday, two people fought for a long time.
In the movie, the hero will fight the villain.
I took a picture of them fighting.

examples.ko: 서로 붙잡고 격투하다가 둘 다 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: They grabbed each other, struggled, and both fell down.
Only after fighting for a good while did the two make up.

explain: '격투하다'는 맨몸으로 서로 치고받으며 싸울 때 써요. 말다툼은 '싸우다'나 '다투다'라고 하고, 운동 경기는 '시합하다'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '몸싸움하다'를 더 자주 들어요.
explain_en: 격투하다 is for fighting with bare hands, trading blows. A verbal quarrel is 싸우다 or 다투다, and a sports match is 시합하다. In daily talk 몸싸움하다 is heard more often.

en: miss a game; sit out (due to injury, etc.)

examples.en: The captain will sit out the next game due to injury.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 두 달 동안 결장했어요.
examples.en: That player was out for two months.

examples.ko: 에이스가 결장할 때 팀 성적이 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The team's results dropped when the ace was out.
Many players are missing games because of colds.
He came back to the stadium for the first time after being out.

examples.ko: 그가 결장한 경기에서 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team won the game he missed.

explain: 스포츠 뉴스에서 선수가 부상이나 징계로 경기에 나오지 못할 때 써요. 반대말은 '출전하다'예요. 학교나 모임에 안 나오는 건 '결석하다', '불참하다'라고 하고 '결장하다'는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In sports news it is for a player who cannot play because of injury or suspension. The opposite is '출전하다'. Not showing up at school or a meeting is '결석하다' or '불참하다'; '결장하다' is not used for that.

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨가 밤새 고함쳐서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The man next door yelled all night, so I couldn't sleep.
The child was startled and suddenly shouted.
Don't yell like that, speak calmly.

examples.ko: 경기장에서 사람들이 목이 터져라 고함치고 있어요.
examples.en: People in the stadium are shouting at the top of their lungs.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 부모님께 고함치면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you're angry, you shouldn't yell at your parents.

examples.ko: 누가 고함치는 소리가 들려서 밖으로 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard someone shouting, so I went outside to check.

explain: '소리를 지르다'가 더 일상적인 말이고, '고함치다'는 화가 나거나 급해서 크게 외친다는 느낌이 강해요. 놀라거나 아파서 지르는 소리는 '비명'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: '소리를 지르다' is the more everyday expression, while '고함치다' strongly suggests shouting out of anger or urgency. A cry from fright or pain is a '비명' (scream), which is a separate word.

examples.en: People let out wild screams while riding the amusement ride.

examples.ko: 밤에 이상한 괴성이 들려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I heard a strange shriek at night and couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 괴성을 내며 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The child is angry and running around shrieking.

examples.ko: 공연장에서 팬들이 괴성에 가까운 환호를 보냈어요.
examples.en: At the concert, fans cheered in near-shrieks.
There were weird screams from the next room, so I called the management office.

examples.ko: 영화 속 괴물이 괴성을 지르며 나타났어요.
examples.en: The monster in the movie appeared letting out a roar.

explain: '괴성을 지르다', '괴성을 내다'처럼 말해요. '비명'이 놀라거나 아파서 나오는 소리라면, '괴성'은 평범하지 않게 크고 날카로운 소리이고 신나거나 화날 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '괴성을 지르다' or '괴성을 내다'. While '비명' is a scream from fear or pain, '괴성' is an unusually loud, sharp sound that can come from excitement or anger too.

examples.en: My younger sibling keeps grumbling that they don't want to do homework.
What are you grumbling about all by yourself?
He went out, muttering complaints, and closed the door.

examples.ko: 구시렁거리지 말고 할 말이 있으면 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter; if you have something to say, say it out loud.
I can hear my grandmother grumbling to herself.
It was Monday morning, so everyone grumbled their way to work.

explain: 못마땅해서 작은 소리로 혼잣말처럼 불평하는 모습이에요. '불평하다'는 분명하게 말하는 느낌이지만, 이 말은 알아듣기 어렵게 중얼거리는 느낌이 있어요. '구시렁대다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes muttering complaints under your breath, as if talking to yourself. '불평하다' sounds like complaining clearly, while this one has a feel of mumbling so that it's hard to make out. It can also be said as '구시렁대다'.

examples.en: The enemy launched a surprise attack on the village at dawn.

examples.ko: 경찰이 밤에 창고를 기습해서 범인을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The police raided the warehouse at night and caught the culprit.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 우리 진영을 기습하는 바람에 졌어요.
examples.en: We lost because the other team hit our side by surprise.

examples.ko: 그들이 기습할 거라고는 아무도 생각하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Nobody expected that they would attack by surprise.
The cat pounced on the toy as if ambushing it.

examples.ko: 군대는 비 오는 날을 노려 기습하고 도망갔어요.
examples.en: The army chose a rainy day, struck by surprise and fled.

explain: '공격하다'는 그냥 치는 것이고, '기습하다'는 상대가 준비하지 못한 때를 노려요. 주로 뉴스나 이야기에서 '~을/를 기습하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: '공격하다' just means to attack, while '기습하다' means to strike when the other side is not ready. It mostly appears in news and stories, in the pattern '~을/를 기습하다'.

examples.en: An angry customer made a scene in the shop.

examples.ko: 제발 오늘 회의에서 깽판 놓지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't wreck the meeting today.

examples.ko: 네가 깽판 쳐서 계획이 다 엉망이 됐어요.
examples.en: You messed it up, and now the whole plan is a wreck.

examples.ko: 일부러 깽판 놓으려고 온 사람 같아요.
examples.en: He seems like someone who came on purpose to cause trouble.

examples.ko: 동생이 방에서 깽판을 친 걸 엄마가 보셨어요.
examples.en: Mom saw that my little brother had trashed the room.
A ruckus broke out at the party and everyone was shocked.

explain: '깽판을 치다', '깽판을 놓다'처럼 거의 이 형태로 써요. 일이 잘 안 되게 망치거나 소란을 피울 때 쓰는 구어체라서 친구나 가족 사이에서 자연스럽고, 격식 있는 자리에서는 '망치다'나 '소란을 피우다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in the forms '깽판을 치다' and '깽판을 놓다'. It is colloquial for ruining something or causing a ruckus, so it fits among friends and family. In formal settings people say '망치다' or '소란을 피우다'.

examples.en: The puppy is whining in front of the door.
I grunted and struggled carrying the heavy box by myself.
The homework is hard, so I've been struggling with it for an hour.
Stop straining by yourself and let's lift it together.
The baby puppy whimpers as it looks for its mother.
I huffed and puffed up the stairs carrying the luggage.

explain: 강아지가 내는 낑낑 소리에도 쓰고, 사람이 힘들게 애쓰는 모습에도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 '끙끙대다'보다 힘을 쓰느라 소리를 내는 느낌이 강해요. '낑낑거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It can describe the whimpering sound a puppy makes, and also a person struggling hard at something. Used for people, it suggests straining and making noise from effort, more so than '끙끙대다'. '낑낑거리다' means the same.

examples.ko: 동생이 설거지 시간만 되면 슬쩍 내빼요.
examples.en: My younger sibling slips away whenever it's time to wash dishes.

examples.ko: 친구가 계산할 때가 되자 어느새 내뺐어요.
examples.en: When it came time to pay, my friend had already slipped away.

examples.ko: 사고를 내고 그냥 내빼면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cause an accident and just run off.

examples.ko: 고양이가 사람을 보자마자 담 너머로 내빼는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a cat dash over the wall as soon as it saw a person.

examples.ko: 일이 힘들다고 혼자 내빼지 말고 같이 해요.
examples.en: Don't bail out on your own just because the work is hard; let's do it together.

examples.ko: 몰래 내빼려고 했는데 선생님한테 딱 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I tried to sneak away, but the teacher caught me.

explain: '도망가다'보다 훨씬 구어적이고, 곤란한 일이나 책임에서 슬쩍 빠져나갈 때 자주 써요. 친구나 가족 사이의 편한 말투에 어울려서 격식 있는 글에는 잘 안 써요. 진짜 무서워서 달아나는 상황이면 '도망가다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is much more colloquial than '도망가다' and is often used when someone slips out of a tough job or responsibility. It suits casual talk among friends or family and is rarely used in formal writing. For truly fleeing in fear, '도망가다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: He made a phone call in a rush.
The child called his mother urgently.
I fell while running in a hurry.
My friend asked me urgently for help.
The firefighters rushed urgently to the scene.
I opened the door hurriedly, but nobody was there.

explain: 일이 급해서 마음의 여유가 없는 모습을 말해요. '급히'는 속도나 시간이 급할 때도 쓰지만, '다급히'는 마음이 몹시 급하고 조급한 느낌이 더 강해요. 주로 부르다, 뛰다, 말하다 같은 동작과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes acting with no room to breathe because things are pressing. '급히' can mean just quick, but '다급히' feels more anxious and desperate. It is typically used with actions like calling, running or speaking.

examples.en: I was tired yesterday, so I slept soundly.
The baby fell into a sweet sleep in its mother's arms.

examples.ko: 단잠 자는 아이를 깨우기 싫어서 조용히 나왔어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to wake the sleeping child, so I left quietly.
On the holiday morning, I enjoyed sleeping soundly until late.
I felt refreshed after waking from a deep sleep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 소리를 들으면서 단잠에 들었어요.
examples.en: Listening to the sound of rain, I drifted into a sound sleep.

explain: 달고 깊게 푹 자는 잠이에요. 보통 '단잠을 자다', '단잠에 빠지다', '단잠을 깨우다'처럼 써요. 말할 때는 '꿀잠'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is sweet, deep, restful sleep. It is typically used as '단잠을 자다', '단잠에 빠지다' or '단잠을 깨우다'. In casual speech people also say '꿀잠'.

examples.en: Someone is clattering dishes in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 주머니 속 동전이 걸을 때마다 달그락대요.
examples.en: The coins in my pocket rattle every time I walk.
Since morning, there has been a clattering sound from next door.
I clattered around washing dishes, and the baby woke up.
Please tidy up quietly without clattering.
The child is putting away toys, making a clatter.

explain: '달그락거리다'와 거의 같고 말할 때는 둘 다 써요. 소리를 내는 주어는 물건일 수도, 물건을 만지는 사람일 수도 있어요. 더 큰 소리는 '덜그럭대다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '달그락거리다', and people use both when speaking. The subject can be the objects or the person handling them. For a bigger sound, you say '덜그럭대다'.

examples.en: The puppy rolls around on the floor.
The ball rolled down the hill.
My stomach hurt so much I felt like rolling around.
The baby plays rolling around on the bed.

examples.ko: 도토리가 대굴대굴 굴러서 잡을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The acorn rolled away and I couldn't catch it.
The marble rolls around on the desk.

explain: 작고 단단한 것이 구르는 모양을 흉내 낸 말이에요. 보통 '대굴대굴 구르다', '대굴대굴 굴러가다'로 써요. '데굴데굴'과 같은 계열이라 소리와 느낌이 비슷해요.
explain_en: It imitates the way something small and hard rolls. It is usually used as '대굴대굴 구르다' or '대굴대굴 굴러가다'. It belongs to the same family as '데굴데굴', so the sound and feel are similar.

examples.en: The ball rolled down the hill.
The child is rolling around on the bed.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 아파서 바닥에서 데굴데굴 굴렀어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt so much that I rolled around on the floor.
The apples tumbled out of the bag, rolling.
The puppy is rolling around on the lawn.
It was so funny I almost rolled on the floor laughing.

explain: 둥글고 큰 것이 계속 구르는 모양이에요. 보통 '데굴데굴 구르다/굴러가다'로 써요. 더 센 느낌은 '떼굴떼굴', 작은 것에는 '대굴대굴'을 써요.
explain_en: It describes something round and fairly large rolling continuously, usually as '데굴데굴 구르다/굴러가다'. '떼굴떼굴' is a stronger version, and '대굴대굴' is used for smaller things.

examples.ko: 돌발 상황이 생겨서 회의가 잠깐 멈췄어요.
examples.en: An unexpected situation came up, so the meeting paused for a moment.

examples.ko: 공연 중에 돌발 사고가 있었지만 무사히 끝났어요.
examples.en: There was a sudden accident during the show, but it ended safely.

examples.ko: 아이의 돌발 행동에 선생님이 깜짝 놀라셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher was startled by the child's sudden behavior.

examples.ko: 여행에서는 돌발 변수에 대비해 여유를 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On a trip, it's good to leave some slack for unexpected variables.
Even though he is a new employee, he answered the unexpected question calmly.

examples.ko: 돌발적인 행동은 위험할 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: Sudden, impulsive behavior can be dangerous, so be careful.

explain: 거의 '돌발 상황', '돌발 행동', '돌발 질문'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 예상하지 못한 일이 갑자기 일어났다는 느낌이고, '돌발적'으로도 말해요. 단순한 '갑작스럽다'보다 문제나 변수라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always followed by a noun, as in '돌발 상황', '돌발 행동', and '돌발 질문'. It means something unexpected suddenly happened, and you can also say '돌발적'. Compared with plain '갑작스럽다', it often carries a sense of a problem or variable.

examples.en: The little bell jingles every time the door opens.

examples.ko: 고양이 목에 단 방울이 딸랑거리는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the bell on the cat's neck jingling.
The coins jingle in my pocket, so it's noisy.

examples.ko: 가게 문이 딸랑거리면 손님이 온 거예요.
examples.en: When the shop door jingles, a customer has come in.

examples.ko: 썰매 종이 딸랑거릴 때마다 아이들이 웃었어요.
examples.en: Every time the sleigh bell jingled, the children laughed.
A bicycle went past with its bell jingling.

explain: 작은 방울, 종, 동전처럼 가볍고 맑은 소리가 날 때 써요. '딸랑대다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 소리 자체는 '딸랑딸랑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it for light, clear sounds from small bells, chimes, or coins. '딸랑대다' means the same thing, and the sound itself is '딸랑딸랑'.

examples.ko: 그는 할 말이 있는 듯 문 앞에서 머뭇댔어요.
examples.en: He hesitated at the door as if he had something to say.

examples.ko: 왜 이렇게 머뭇대요? 빨리 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Why are you hesitating so much? Just say it.

examples.ko: 질문을 받자 아이는 대답을 못 하고 머뭇대기만 했어요.
examples.en: When asked the question, the child couldn't answer and just hesitated.

examples.ko: 머뭇대지 말고 마음먹은 대로 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't hesitate; do what you've decided.

examples.ko: 길에서 머뭇대는 외국인에게 먼저 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I spoke first to the foreigner who was hesitating on the street.

examples.ko: 고백할까 말까 한참 머뭇대다가 그냥 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I wavered for a long time about confessing, then just went back.

explain: '머뭇거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 말을 할까 말까, 움직일까 말까 망설이는 모습에 쓰고, '머뭇대지 말고'처럼 재촉할 때도 많이 써요. 반대로 망설이지 않을 때는 '주저 없이', '망설임 없이'라고 해요.
explain_en: You can swap it with '머뭇거리다', which means the same. It shows hesitating over whether to speak or move, and it is often used to urge someone, as in '머뭇대지 말고'. When someone doesn't hesitate, you say '주저 없이' or '망설임 없이'.

examples.ko: 가방 속에서 빵이 눌려서 뭉개진 채로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The bread got pressed in my bag and came out squashed.
It rained, and my makeup got completely smudged.
If you enlarge the photo a lot, the letters get blurry.

examples.ko: 딸기가 뭉개지지 않게 조심히 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please carry the strawberries carefully so they don't get squashed.
The cake lost its shape, so I made it again.

examples.ko: 발에 밟힌 꽃이 땅에 뭉개져 있어요.
examples.en: The flower stepped on is squashed on the ground.

explain: 눌리거나 밟혀서 모양이 망가질 때 써요. 화장이 번지거나 사진·글씨가 흐릿해질 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 능동형 '뭉개다'는 '일을 미적거리다'라는 뜻으로도 써서, 이 단어와 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요.
explain_en: It is used when something loses its shape by being pressed or stepped on. It can also be used when makeup smudges or when a photo or text becomes blurry. The active form '뭉개다' is also used to mean putting off a task, so be careful not to confuse the two.

examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and smashed.
My phone screen is smashed.

examples.ko: 커피잔이 박살 나는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by the sound of the coffee cup smashing.
My dream was shattered, and I had a hard time for a while.

examples.ko: 박살 난 유리 조각을 조심해서 치웠어요.
examples.en: I carefully cleaned up the pieces of smashed glass.

examples.ko: 계획이 박살 날 뻔했지만 친구가 도와줬어요.
examples.en: The plan almost fell apart, but my friend helped.

explain: '박살이 나다'는 물건이 산산이 부서질 때, '박살 내다'는 부수거나 크게 이길 때 써요. 말투가 거칠어서 뉴스나 격식 있는 글에서는 '파손되다', '크게 이기다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 상대 팀을 박살 냈어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 부술 때뿐 아니라 시합에서 크게 이길 때도 써요. 말투가 거칠어서 친한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for breaking objects but also for winning a game by a big margin. The tone is rough, so it suits close friends.

explain_en: '박살이 나다' is for things breaking into pieces, and '박살 내다' is for smashing something or winning big. The tone is rough, so news and formal writing use words like '파손되다' or '크게 이기다' instead.

examples.en: That empty house has been left unattended for a long time.
A bicycle had been left by the roadside.
A neglected building can be dangerous.
If a wound is neglected, it gets worse.
The puppy that had been neglected met a new family.

examples.ko: 공원에 쓰레기가 방치되지 않도록 매일 치워요.
examples.en: We clean every day so trash is not left in the park.

explain: 돌봐 주는 사람이 없어서 그냥 놓여 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요. '방치하다'와 달리 놓인 물건이나 사람이 주인공이에요. '버려지다'처럼 완전히 버린 건 아니지만 아무도 신경 쓰지 않았다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it for a state of being left as is because no one looks after it. Unlike '방치하다', the thing or person left behind is the subject. It is not fully abandoned like '버려지다', but it feels like nobody paid attention.

en: feel sore from pressure; can't help (doing)

examples.ko: 바닥이 너무 딱딱해서 등이 많이 배겨요.
examples.en: The floor is so hard that my back really hurts.
After sitting for a long time, my bottom got sore.

examples.ko: 신발 속 돌 때문에 발바닥이 배겨서 걸을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: A stone in my shoe is digging into my foot, so I can't walk.

examples.ko: 이 매트를 깔면 바닥이 덜 배길 거예요.
examples.en: If you lay this mat down, the floor will be less hard on you.

examples.ko: 이렇게 졸라 대는데 안 사 주고 배기겠어요?
examples.en: When they nag this much, how could I not buy it for them?

examples.ko: 이렇게 맛있는 걸 보고 안 먹고 배기는 사람이 있을까요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who could see food this tasty and not eat it?

explain: 딱딱한 바닥이나 물건에 눌려서 아플 때 '등이/엉덩이가/발바닥이 배기다'라고 말해요. 이때는 '아프다'보다 눌려서 배긴다는 느낌이 있어요. '못 배기다', '-고는 못 배기다'는 '참을 수 없다'는 뜻으로 따로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 노래를 들으면 따라 부르지 않고는 못 배겨요.
phrases.en: When I hear that song, I can't help singing along.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않고는 못 배기다' 꼴로 '하고 싶은 마음을 참을 수 없다'는 뜻이 돼요. 몸이 배겨서 아픈 것과는 다른 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the form '-지 않고는 못 배기다' it means you cannot hold back the urge to do something. It is different from the physical sense of being sore from pressure.

explain_en: When you are pressed by a hard floor or object and it hurts, you say things like '등이/엉덩이가/발바닥이 배기다'. It feels more like being dug into than a plain '아프다'. '못 배기다' and '-고는 못 배기다' are also used separately to mean you cannot stand or resist something.

examples.en: The children are spinning round and round on the playground.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타고 나니 세상이 뱅글뱅글 돌아요.
examples.en: After the ride, the world is spinning around me.
The top spins nicely round and round on the floor.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 같은 자리를 뱅글뱅글 걸으며 전화를 받았어요.
examples.en: He walked round and round the same spot while taking the call.

examples.ko: 머리가 아파서 방이 뱅글뱅글 도는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My head hurts and the room feels like it is spinning.
The puppy spins round and round trying to catch its tail.

explain: '빙글빙글'보다 작고 가벼운 느낌이라 작은 물건이나 아이, 강아지의 움직임에 잘 어울려요. 거의 항상 '돌다'와 함께 쓰고, 어지러울 때 세상이 도는 느낌에도 써요.
explain_en: It feels smaller and lighter than '빙글빙글', so it suits small objects, children and puppies. It is almost always used with '돌다' (to turn), and also for the feeling that the world is spinning when you are dizzy.

examples.en: The whole family is bustling around because guests are coming.
The kids are playing noisily in the yard.

examples.ko: 시험 날 아침부터 집 안이 법석거렸어요.
examples.en: The house was in a flurry from the morning of the exam.
It's nothing serious, so why are you making such a fuss?
We bustled around all day getting ready for the move.
The market is so bustling with people that my head is spinning.

explain: 여럿이 시끄럽고 바쁘게 움직이거나, 별일 아닌데 좀 지나치게 호들갑을 떠는 느낌이에요. '법석대다', '법석이다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '법석을 떨다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It describes people moving around noisily and busily, or making a bit too much fuss over something minor. '법석대다' and '법석이다' mean the same thing. In daily speech, '법석을 떨다' is also widely used.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어서 봉변을 당할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong turn and almost ran into trouble.

examples.ko: 낯선 곳에서 혼자 다니다 봉변당하지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get into trouble walking alone in an unfamiliar place.

examples.ko: 그 사람 때문에 친구들 앞에서 큰 봉변을 겪었어요.
examples.en: Because of that person, I went through a real humiliation in front of my friends.
I thought it was an unfair humiliation, so I got angry.

examples.ko: 공연장에서 아무 봉변 없이 무사히 나왔어요.
examples.en: I got out of the concert hall safely without any trouble.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 첫날 상사에게 큰 봉변을 당했어요.
examples.en: On the first day, the new employee suffered a nasty humiliation at the hands of the boss.

explain: 내 잘못보다 남 때문에 갑자기 당하는 망신이나 낭패에 주로 써요. '봉변을 당하다', '봉변을 겪다'처럼 쓰고, 말로 당하는 모욕에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for sudden humiliation or trouble caused by someone else rather than your own mistake. It appears as '봉변을 당하다' or '봉변을 겪다', and can cover verbal insults too.

examples.ko: 길 한복판에서 두 사람이 서로 삿대질을 하며 싸웠어요.
examples.en: Two people were fighting in the middle of the street, jabbing fingers at each other.

examples.ko: 회의 중에는 삿대질 말고 차분하게 이야기해 주세요.
examples.en: Please talk calmly during the meeting instead of pointing fingers.
The man even jabbed his finger at me, so I was really scared.
It started as a quarrel, but before long they were jabbing fingers at each other.

examples.ko: 아이 앞에서 삿대질로 화를 내면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't show anger by wagging your finger in front of a child.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 삿대질을 하다가 경찰에게 주의를 받았어요.
examples.en: He was warned by the police for pointing his finger aggressively.

explain: '손가락질'은 누군가를 가리키거나 비난할 때도 두루 쓰지만, '삿대질'은 화가 나서 상대 얼굴 쪽으로 손가락을 내밀며 다툴 때 써요. 보통 '삿대질을 하다', '삿대질이 오가다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '손가락질' can be used broadly for pointing at or blaming someone, but '삿대질' is for jabbing a finger toward someone's face in anger during a fight. It usually appears as '삿대질을 하다' or '삿대질이 오가다'.

examples.ko: 비가 갑자기 와서 다들 생난리가 났어요.
examples.en: It suddenly rained, and everyone was in an uproar.
The child threw a huge fit in front of the store.
It's nothing serious, so why such a fuss?
When the singer showed up, the airport was in total chaos.
After a whole lot of chaos, I finally got on the bus.
My younger sibling shouted as if a huge commotion had broken out.

explain: 그냥 '난리'보다 괜히 필요 이상으로 소란스럽다는 느낌이 있어요. '생떼', '생고생'처럼 '생-'이 붙으면 억지스럽고 불필요한 느낌이 더해지고, '생난리를 치다/나다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '난리', it feels like a needlessly big commotion. As in '생떼' and '생고생', the '생-' adds a sense of unnecessary or forced, and it is often used as '생난리를 치다/나다'.

examples.ko: 버스에서 선잠이 들어서 정류장을 놓칠 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I dozed off on the bus and almost missed my stop.
The baby sleeps lightly and keeps waking up.
I only slept lightly last night, so I'm very tired.
I napped on the sofa and now my neck hurts.
When I woke from my light sleep, it was already morning.
The sound of thunder woke me from my light sleep.

explain: 깊이 들지 못한 얕은 잠이라서 '선잠을 자다', '선잠이 들다', '선잠이 깨다'처럼 써요. 반대는 '깊은 잠'이고, 낮에 잠깐 자는 '낮잠'과는 시간이 아니라 잠의 깊이를 말해요.
explain_en: It is shallow sleep that never gets deep, used as '선잠을 자다', '선잠이 들다' and '선잠이 깨다'. Its opposite is '깊은 잠' (deep sleep), and unlike '낮잠' (daytime nap) it describes how deep the sleep is, not when it happens.

examples.en: Two friends are whispering in the back.

examples.ko: 수업 중에 소곤거리면 선생님이 다 들으세요.
examples.en: If you whisper during class, the teacher hears everything.
The child whispered into my ear.
In the library you should talk in whispers.
What are you two whispering about?
I heard whispering and looked back.

explain: 남이 못 듣게 작은 소리로 계속 말하는 모습이에요. '소곤대다'라고도 해요. 남을 흉보듯 몰래 말하는 느낌이 강하면 '수군거리다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes talking continuously in a small voice so others can't hear. You can also say '소곤대다'. When the feeling is more of secretly gossiping about someone, '수군거리다' is sometimes used.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 송전이 끊겨서 마을이 어두워졌어요.
examples.en: The power transmission was cut by the typhoon, so the village went dark.

examples.ko: 산에 송전탑을 세우는 문제로 주민들이 반대해요.
examples.en: Residents are opposing the plan to build power transmission towers on the mountain.

examples.ko: 발전소에서 도시까지 송전하는 데 선이 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: Many lines are needed to transmit power from the plant to the city.
There was a blackout because they were inspecting the transmission facilities.

examples.ko: 먼 곳으로 송전할 때 전기가 조금 손실돼요.
examples.en: Some electricity is lost when transmitting it over long distances.
Work on the power transmission lines starts tomorrow.

explain: 집에서는 '전기가 들어오다/끊기다'라고 하고, '송전'은 뉴스와 공사 이야기에서 써요. '송전탑', '송전선', '송전 중단'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요. 전기를 만드는 '발전'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: At home people say '전기가 들어오다/끊기다', while '송전' belongs to news and construction talk. It often appears in compounds like '송전탑', '송전선' and '송전 중단'. It helps to remember it as a pair with '발전' (generating power).
